issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Ride with two private attributes (-name: String, -abbreviation: char) which implies both attributes should be private. In the solution repository Ride.java, the field name is declared public (public String name;), while abbreviation is private. This is a visibility mismatch between the specification (UML/problem statement) and the provided solution. Students expecting to follow the UML (i.e., declare attributes private and provide public getters) may be confused by the public name field in the solution and by any tests or examples that assume encapsulation.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the visibility of Ride.name consistent with the UML by declaring the field private (private String name;) and keep the public getter getName(). Alternatively, if the intention was to expose the field publicly, update the UML and problem text to indicate that 'name' should be public. The recommended fix to preserve encapsulation and match the UML/specification is to change the solution's 'public String name;' to 'private String name;'.
